publisher: World Bank (World Development Indicators); source organisation: WHO data, supplemented by country data
title: Hospital beds (per 1,000 people), SH.MED.BEDS.ZS, India
licence: CC BY 4.0 (World Bank open data terms)
method: All non-null annual values for India copied from the World Bank API (dataset last updated 2026-10-08). Values with floating-point noise (1960-1991) rounded to 4 decimals; 2000-2021 values are printed to 2 decimals and copied as is.
limitations: Covers public and private inpatient beds (World Bank definition). The 2000-2021 values fall smoothly every year (2.13 to 1.59), which suggests modelled or interpolated figures rather than yearly counts; the source does not say. Large unexplained jump between 1991 (0.787) and 2000 (2.13): flagged as a break. No state-level data. No WHO norm for hospital beds is recorded because no official WHO document stating one was found.

publisher: World Health Organization, Global Health Observatory (National Health Workforce Accounts data portal, December 2025 update)
title: Medical doctors (per 10,000), HWF_0001, India
licence: WHO GHO data; reuse with attribution to WHO under WHO terms of use (no licence stated in the API response)
method: All annual values for India copied exactly from the WHO GHO OData API ('Value' field). WHO's matching count series HWF_0002 gives 1,349,679 doctors for 2023, the same figure as the National Medical Commission count of MBBS doctors registered up to 31.12.2022 printed in National Health Profile 2023 Table 5.1, so the series is based on cumulative registrations.
limitations: Based on registered doctors (cumulative registrations with state medical councils/NMC), which include doctors who have died, retired, emigrated or are registered in more than one state; not a count of active doctors. Allopathic (modern medicine) only; AYUSH practitioners excluded. 1991 value (12.31) is far above 1995 (4.79) with no explanation from WHO: break flagged at 1995. 2011 (7.31) is out of line with 2010 and 2012.

publisher: World Health Organization, Global Health Observatory (National Health Workforce Accounts data portal, December 2025 update)
title: Nursing and midwifery personnel (per 10,000), HWF_0006, India
licence: WHO GHO data; reuse with attribution to WHO under WHO terms of use (no licence stated in the API response)
method: All annual values for India copied exactly from the WHO GHO OData API ('Value' field).
limitations: Based on registration data (nursing and midwifery councils), not on active workforce. 2018 (17.0) is well below 2017 (21.82) and 2020 (23.27) and is likely a reporting change; WHO gives no note. No values for 2013 and 2019.

publisher: World Health Organization, Global Health Observatory; sum calculated by Tathya
title: Medical doctors (HWF_0001) plus nursing and midwifery personnel (HWF_0006), per 10,000, India
licence: WHO GHO data; reuse with attribution to WHO under WHO terms of use (no licence stated in the API response)
method: For each year in which WHO publishes both series, Tathya adds the published doctors density (HWF_0001) and nursing and midwifery density (HWF_0006). Both use the same WHO population denominator. The two inputs are written in each row's note. Second input URL: https://ghoapi.azureedge.net/api/HWF_0006?$filter=SpatialDim%20eq%20'IND'
limitations: Sum of rounded published values (may differ from an exact calculation by 0.01). Inherits the registration basis of both series and the 2018 nursing outlier. This is the aggregate that WHO's 44.5 per 10,000 SDG index threshold refers to (physicians, nurses and midwives).

publisher: World Health Organization
title: Global strategy on human resources for health: Workforce 2030 (2016), Annex 1
licence: © World Health Organization 2016
method: Benchmark only, no data rows. Annex 1 (PDF page 42) states that 'an indicative threshold of an aggregate density of 4.45 physicians, nurses and midwives per 1000 population was identified' (= 44.5 per 10,000), the median of SDG tracer indicator attainment.
coverage: Benchmark value used in the indicator definitions of doctors_per_10000 and health_workers_per_10000
limitations: WHO calls it an indicative threshold used for needs-based workforce estimates, not a mandatory norm. It covers doctors, nurses and midwives together, not doctors alone.
